headline: I am currently serving as the 'World's Eternal Grocery Coordinator' after a store clerk joked about my shopping habits
body:
It started as a simple request for a bag of potatoes at my local neighborhood kirana, but now I find myself officially ‘The Eternal Potato Procurer’ for the entire sector. The store owner, in a fit of over-enthusiastic customer service, printed a laminated badge with my name and that exact title after I jokingly remarked that I come here every single day for my starch fix. Now, I cannot even walk past the shop without residents pressing their handwritten grocery lists into my palms, assuming I have been appointed by some unseen authority to manage the regional inventory.

My life has become a blur of pulse-weighing and pulse-checking. Just yesterday, a man pulled me aside in the parking lot to protest the fluctuating prices of onions, demanding to know what my long-term strategy was for the upcoming festive season. I tried to explain that I am a freelance architect with no actual oversight of supply chains, but he just nodded sagely and said, ‘That is exactly what a high-level trade official would say.’

I’ve tried to stop wearing the badge, but the shopkeeper keeps taping a new one onto my shirt whenever I enter. I suppose there are worse fates than being recognized as the supreme authority on dairy availability, but I do wish I could just buy a pack of biscuits without having to negotiate a bilateral trade agreement with the woman in line behind me who wants to swap her flour for my butter.
caption: Being a ‘minister for life’ sounds cool until you’re solely responsible for the neighborhood’s milk shortage. I just wanted potatoes. #EternalCoordinator #GroceryPolitics #BureaucracyLife (satire)
igHook: Would you accept a lifetime title if it meant you had to solve everyone's shopping problems?
imagePrompt: A close-up, slightly out-of-focus shot of a hand wearing a makeshift, hand-drawn name badge pinned to a shirt, standing in a busy and colorful neighborhood grocery store.

sourceHeadline.title: Piyush Goyal gets a ‘trade minister for life’ tag from US trade chief at G20

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 0 is the most successful because it grounds the absurdity in a specific, relatable setting (the neighborhood kirana) and uses concrete details like pulse-weighing and the shopkeeper taping badges on the protagonist, which provides a vivid, humorous image. While the 'forced into a title' premise appears frequently, this version maintains a consistent, deadpan tone and avoids the repetitive 'HR/diplomat' jargon found in other candidates.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article is a harmless, absurd piece of fiction centered on a relatable, non-identifiable individual. It does not name any real public figures, private citizens, or protected groups, and the image prompt is sufficiently generic.
